chapter: Chicago radio, Whiteman and courting Mildred
title: Meeting Mildred and backing the afternoon shows
summary: At NBC Chicago his band accompanies Mildred, Johnny Fulton and the new Rhythm Boys; he tells her he first heard her on the radio.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: -- they had taken studios there. So, but those two shows, the people like [Senkeny,] and Robb and people who were head of NBC in Chicago, at that time, Whiteman just put me right in with Jules. We had a six -- I guess it was six-seven piece band. And we just -- piano, bass and drums and all that sort of thing. And finally, Dave Rose came in. As a regular piano player. So that's when I met Mildred. She and oh, Johnny Fulton and The Rhythm Boys would do afternoon shows.
So we used to play for Mildred.
Yeah. She did a three times a week -- I think it was three times a week show, Johnny Fulton did a three times a week show and the Rhythm Boys did a show. Not Bing Crosby,
but the new Rhythm Boys, -- Oh.
-- because Bing and Al and Harry Berris Arnhem has left and stayed with Gus Arnheim, on the coast.
So they had -- he picked up a quart -- it was really a quartet, but it was -- they called it the Rhythm Boys --
And they worked at WBBM in Chicago.
And they used to sing behind Mildred --

Well, I'll be darned. Well -- like you -- so we'll talk about that a minute, because that's -- that's very interesting, you know, you'd said you heard Mildred on the air, when you were in Milwaukee -- when you -- you know --
And you said you never heard anything so beautiful, etc.
You fell in love with her before you ever met her. So, then you must've been terribly thrilled when you found out you were going to back her --
Yeah. So I told her I used to listen to her in -- on the radio when she was on the Old Gold Show. And --
